headline: South Asia: Heavy fighting, internet disruption as Ethiopia conflict rages
script:
Good afternoon. This is your global conflict briefing.

BOTTOM LINE UP FRONT:
- South Asia: Heavy fighting, internet disruption as Ethiopia conflict rages.
- Asia: France to protect key Saudi oil terminal as Houthis step up missile attacks.
- Western Russia: Two Russian guided bombs hit different districts of Sumy: several injured.

Full breakdown follows.

NORTH AMERICA
United States - bottom line: Military personnel data exposed in breach, agency warns.
- Military Times, one day ago: Military personnel data exposed in breach, agency warns.
Unauthorized users accessed files containing the personal information of U.S. military personnel, a new breach notification letter warns.
- Military Times, 23 hours ago: 8 sailors attempted suicide aboard ships from Lincoln strike group, Cao says.
Acting Navy Secretary Hung Cao confirmed that eight sailors from the USS Abraham Lincoln carrier strike group attempted suicide.
Central America: no notable developments in the last 48 hours.
The Caribbean: no notable developments in the last 48 hours.

SOUTH AMERICA
South America: no notable developments in the last 48 hours.

EUROPE
Western Russia - bottom line: Two Russian guided bombs hit different districts of Sumy: several injured.
- Ukrainska Pravda, 3 hours ago: Two Russian guided bombs hit different districts of Sumy: several injured.
Russian forces attacked Sumy with two guided aerial bombs on 25 September, with strikes recorded in two different districts of the city. Several people were injured and one person was taken to hospital.
- Ukrainska Pravda, 5 hours ago: Ukraine strikes three Russian plants involved in missile production.
Ukraine’s General Staff said its forces struck plants in Tula, Voronezh and Ulyanovsk oblasts involved in rocket fuel, missile and military electronics production.
- Ukrainska Pravda, one hour ago: Number injured in Russian attacks on Kyiv rises to 43, with 5 killed.
Russian drone attacks on Kyiv on 25 September killed five people and injured 43, including two children, with 25 casualties admitted to hospital.
- Ukrainska Pravda, 3 hours ago: Russian drone strikes energy workers' vehicle in Odesa Oblast, killing one person and injuring another – photos.
A Russian drone struck a DTEK vehicle carrying energy workers in Odesa Oblast, killing one employee and injuring another after the vehicle left a substation.
Southern Europe - bottom line: Zelenskyy warns $27B funding gap could leave Ukraine short of weapons.
- Politico Europe, 4 hours ago: Zelenskyy warns $27B funding gap could leave Ukraine short of weapons.
The president said he received a positive and constructive response from the EU during his diplomatic talks this week.
- Balkan Insight, 4 hours ago: Week in Review: Spyware, AI and Arrests.
Tech concerns mount over elections in Serbia, spy chief’s arrest tests Albania’s NATO ties, protests over court verdicts continue in Kosovo and North Macedonia mulls impact of dangerous virus, our selection of Balkan Insight’s Premium stories this week shows.
- Politico Europe, 13 hours ago: Deutschland und Spanien zetteln Papierkrieg zu „Made in Europe“-Auslegung an.
Berlin strebt einen breit aufgestellten Verbund von Handelspartnern an, während Madrid ein gestaffeltes System vorschlägt, bei dem in der EU hergestellte Waren Vorrang genießen.

AFRICA

- Jerusalem Post, Africanews, 2 hours ago: Israeli teenager killed during Russian drone strike on residential building in Kyiv.
The Israeli consulate in Kyiv and the Foreign Ministry are in contact with the teenager's family and assisting in the matter.

Tigray was cut off from the world during the 2020-2022 civil war, which killed around 600,000 people.
- Al Jazeera - Middle East, 5 hours ago: US seeking to revive Russia-Ukraine ceasefire talks.

- Al Jazeera - Middle East, 6 hours ago: Pakistan, Turkiye edge closer towards joining Saudi war against Houthis.
Pakistani and Turkish military chiefs head to Riyadh for urgent talks, but both countries remain cautious on involvement

- AllAfrica - Southern Africa, 4 hours ago: South Africa: Zulu King Breaks Silence On Deadly Heist At His Royal Palace.
[Scrolla] King Misuzulu kaZwelithini condemned a cash heist gang during uMkhosi weLembe commemorations, after an attack at KwaKhangelamankengane Royal Palace killed two Fidelity guards on 7 September. The King used the event, which also marked his 52nd birthday, to renew his call for KwaZulu-Natal to be renamed KwaZulu.

[Nyasa Times] The Taekwondo Association of Malawi (TAM) has organised awareness games to take place on Saturday, 26 September, at Chichiri Shopping Mall car park from 9am to 12:30pm.
- AllAfrica - Southern Africa, one hour ago: Malawi: Prophet Kambale's Life International Church Marks a Decade With Groundbreaking Ceremony.
[Nyasa Times] There is a particular kind of energy that builds around a church anniversary when the milestone is not simply looking backwards but breaking ground on something new. That was the atmosphere at Mbinzi Secondary School Hall in Area 3, Lilongwe, where Life International Church (LIC), founded by Prophet Amos Kambale, marked a decade of ministry with a two-day Total Transformation Conference that doubled as the launch of its next chapter altogether.

[New Era] One of the compelling factors which sent many Namibians into exile to wage the war of the liberation struggle was land acquisition.
Africa - bottom line: Analyst warns Ethiopia fighting could widen into regional conflict.
- Africanews, 3 hours ago: Analyst warns Ethiopia fighting could widen into regional conflict.
Renewed fighting in northern Ethiopia could spread beyond Tigray and destabilize the wider Horn of Africa, an International Crisis Group analyst warned
- AllAfrica - Conflict, 10 hours ago: Sudan: Nuba Christian and Muslim Leaders Call for End to Sudan War.

- Africanews, 12 hours ago: Ethiopian president warns of 'interference' amid renewed Tigray fighting.
Speaking at the UN General Assembly, Taye Atske Selassie blamed 'external actors' for renewed conflict in the region.
- Africanews, one hour ago: Common and Public Enemy honoured at Black Music Action Coalition Awards.
The Black Music Action Coalition honored rap artists Common and Public Enemy at their 6th annual BMAC Gala Thursday.

ASIA
South Asia - bottom line: Heavy fighting, internet disruption as Ethiopia conflict rages.
- Dawn (Pakistan), 7 hours ago: Heavy fighting, internet disruption as Ethiopia conflict rages.
Ethiopian forces battled overnight to repel an assault by Tigray rebels in the Afar region, a humanitarian source said on Friday, with reports of an internet blackout in the north of the country. Rebels in the northern Tigray region seized local airports and launched attacks into the neighbouring states of Afar and Amhara this week, saying they were once again in a “full-blown war” with the federal government. Locals fear a repeat of the telecoms blackout and supplies blockade imposed on Tigray during the last civil war in 2020-2022 that killed an estimated 600,000 people.
- Dawn (Pakistan), 2 hours ago: Info ministry dismisses Afghan claims of destroying Pakistani post near border in Balochistan as 'fake'.
The information ministry dismissed on Friday claims by the Afghan defence ministry of a Pakistani post having been destroyed near the Spin Boldak border — the frontier between Balochistan and Kandahar — as “fake and fabricated”. The information ministry also took note of Afghan claims that there had been no casualties among the Afghan forces in the latest episode of clash between the two sides. “The claim is fake and fabricated.
- Dawn (Pakistan), The Hindu - International, 10 hours ago: Security forces kill several Afghan Taliban fighters in retaliatory action along Balochistan border: sources.
Pakistani troops responded to an act of aggression along the Pakistan-Afghanistan border in Balochistan and killed several Afghan Taliban on Thursday, state media reported, citing sources. State-run APP reported, citing sources, that the Afghan Taliban attempted to enter the Pakistani territory in Balochistan’s Gulistan sector and carry out an act of aggression. Meanwhile, officials also reported attacks on some border posts in Pakistan. The APP report said in retaliatory action, several Afghan Taliban fighters were killed.
- Dawn (Pakistan), one hour ago: 33 India-sponsored terrorists killed by security forces in Balochistan since Sept 21: ISPR.
Security forces have killed 33 terrorists in counter-terrorism operations in Balochistan since Sept 21, the military’s media affairs wing said in a statement on Friday. Terrorists from Fitna-al-Khawarij and Fitna-al-Hindustan were targeted in the operations, according to the Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR). The state uses the term Fitna al-Khawarij for the banned Tehreek-i-Taliban Pakistan (TTP) and refers to designated Balochistan-based groups as Fitna al-Hindustan to highlight India’s role in terrorism and destabilisation across Pakistan.

President Emmanuel Macron said France would send troops to defend an oil plant in Saudi Arabia as the Iran-backed Houthi militia took responsibility for new attacks on the kingdom. Macron said in a television interview Thursday with TF1 and France 2 that he would send soldiers and military support to help protect the Saudi port of Yanbu. Amid the polished silverware and fine crystal stemware on display at the state dinner in the White House on Thursday sat the vacuum flasks brought by Chinese President Xi Jinping and first lady Peng Liyuan. The couple’s flasks, black for Xi and white for Peng, were spotted on their table during the formal dinner, signalling a subtle self-assurance as cultural authenticity met high diplomacy. Extending this everyday practice to the White House banquet was in tune with the host nation’s own...

The United States and China must work together to establish safety guardrails for artificial intelligence, leading scholars and industry leaders said at a Singapore forum, warning that rapid advances in the technology demand stronger risk controls. Speaking at the FutureChina Business Forum on Friday, Jude Blanchette, managing director of consultancy Macro Advisory Partners, urged the two superpowers to find common ground despite escalating geopolitical tensions. “If ever there was a moment for...
- South China Morning Post - China, 6 hours ago: Young Chinese women sew own underwear, clothes, amid frustration with fast fashion.
Frustrated by low-quality materials, careless craftsmanship, and escalating prices, some young women in China are taking matters into their own hands by learning to sew their own underwear, accessories, and handbags. This summer, a surge of sewing enthusiasts flocked to RedNote to showcase their handmade creations. Many beginners embarked on their journey with underwear, assuming it would be a straightforward first project due to its minimal fabric requirements. However, they quickly encountered...
India - bottom line: Who is Tommy “Gun” McMillen? Meet UFC’s 12-0 featherweight prospect.
- Times of India - Top Stories, 2 hours ago: Who is Tommy “Gun” McMillen? Meet UFC’s 12-0 featherweight prospect.
Tommy 'Gun' McMillen is building his reputation in the UFC featherweight division with an undefeated record. He began his combat sports journey at a young age, excelling in wrestling and boxing. McMillen has won all three of his UFC fights, showcasing his striking and finishing abilities. He broke a UFC record for significant strikes landed in a three-round fight during his bout with Alberto Montes.
- Times of India - Top Stories, 4 hours ago: From Ukraine to Africa, drone dog fights now a reality.
The proliferation of attack drones is prompting militaries worldwide to develop drone interception technologies. Ukraine has become a primary testing ground for interceptor UAVs and innovative technologies. Other nations, including the United States and India, are developing advanced counter-drone systems to address emerging threats. The ongoing arms race in drone technology continues to evolve rapidly with new developments.
- Times of India - Top Stories, 4 hours ago: Trump gives 'totally unacceptable' warning to Xi over China helping Iran.
Donald Trump told Xi Jinping that any assistance China provides to Iran is unacceptable during his visit. The two leaders held a closed-door meeting to discuss various critical global issues, including trade and military matters. Trump organized a state dinner attended by key US technology executives to enhance relations. The visit coincided with China's Mid-Autumn Festival, marking a time for family gatherings and festivities.
- NDTV - Top Stories, 6 hours ago: In 1st Joint Op, Finland, Sweden Deploy Jets To Intercept Russian Aircraft.
The Baltic Sea region, of which the Gulf of Finland is part, is on high alert after incidents involving gas pipeline outages, airspace violations and drone sightings since Russia's 2022 full-scale invasion of Ukraine.

South Korean President Lee Jae Myung on Thursday expressed concern over Volodymyr Zelensky’s public disclosure of the transfer of two North Korean prisoners of war (POWs) to South Korea, saying the Ukrainian president had violated an agreement to keep the move private. In a statement posted on X, Lee took aim at the Ukrainian leader […]

AUSTRALIA
Australia - bottom line: At least eight killed in Ukraine Russia drone strike exchange.
- ABC News Australia, The Moscow Times, 7 hours ago: At least eight killed in Ukraine Russia drone strike exchange.
At least eight people have been killed, including a 14-year-old boy, during drone attacks across Russia and Ukraine.

As the UN warns traditional safeguards are ‘unravelling’, Donald Trump says he will encourage, not restrain, the AI race When the Australian prime minister, Anthony Albanese, sat down for an interview in the heart of Silicon Valley at the weekend he had known for two days that his was the first government known to have been attacked by a rogue AI agent. He didn’t reveal the attack then, but he sounded a warning about the march of AI: “the risk is that AI develops in a way in which humans are no longer in control of what AI is producing.” Continue reading...

There is no excuse for what happened Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast When you get sick, Medicare exists to take care of you. It sits at the centre of a health system that our prime minister rightly calls the envy of the world. It’s one of the few institutions nearly every Australian still trusts. So when an AI company threatens this system, it couldn’t be more serious.
- The Guardian - Australia, 2 hours ago: Bruce Pascoe’s new book may spark another culture war. He hopes for ‘decency and intellectual curiosity’ this time.
The Dark Emu author rails against Christianity, capitalism and colonialism – and Shakespeare and Charles Dickens cop a serve too. He’s ready for blowback On the eve of publication of his new book, Bruce Pascoe is steeling himself for potential controversy that could rival the bitter storm that battered and bruised him for years over the 2014 book that rewrote Australian history: Dark Emu.
